---
title: "Human checking: the next step"
subtitle: "What the two checkers do, why it is done blind, and how the scores appear here"
---

```{r}
source("_common.R", encoding = "UTF-8")
st <- read_status()
rel_sum <- rd("annotation/scores_relevance_summary.csv")
rel_agr <- rd("annotation/scores_relevance_agreement.csv")
rel_q <- rd("annotation/scores_relevance_by_question.csv")
cl_cond <- rd("annotation/scores_claims_by_condition.csv")
cl_agr <- rd("annotation/scores_claims_agreement.csv")
n_rel <- if (!is.null(st)) st$items[st$task == "relevance"][1] else NA
n_cl <- if (!is.null(st)) st$items[st$task == "claims"][1] else NA
done_rel <- if (!is.null(st)) min(st$done[st$task == "relevance"]) else 0
done_cl <- if (!is.null(st)) min(st$done[st$task == "claims"]) else 0
scored <- !is.null(rel_agr) && any(rel_agr$items > 0)
claims_scored <- !is.null(cl_agr) && any(cl_agr$items > 0)
```

::: {.in-short}
**In short.** Computers can show that the three searches find *different* records. Only people
can say whether the records are *useful* for the question, and whether the AI's sentences are
*true to the records*. Two people each judge **`r num(n_rel)` records** and
**`r num(n_cl)` sentences**, without knowing which search they came from.
`r if (!scored) "**This has not been done yet**, which is why all the scores in the result files are empty." else "The scores are shown below."`
:::

## Progress

```{r}
if (!is.null(st)) {
  s <- st
  s$task <- ifelse(s$task == "relevance", "Records (is it useful?)", "Sentences (is it supported?)")
  s$progress <- pct(s$done / s$items)
  tbl(s[, c("task", "sheet", "items", "done", "progress")], c("Task", "Sheet", "Items", "Judged", "Progress"))
} else cat("No checking sheets were found in this run.")
```

## What the checkers do

### Sheet 1: records (`relevance_annotator_1.csv`, `relevance_annotator_2.csv`)

Each row is one record: its title, year, institution, type, language, subject words, and a link
to Finna. The checker reads the research question shown in the same row and writes one number
in the column `relevance_0_1_2`:

| Number | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **2** | Directly useful: the record is about the topic and the period of the question |
| **1** | Partly useful: related topic, period or background, but not direct evidence |
| **0** | Not useful |

Every record appears **only once**, even if two or three searches found it, so nobody judges
the same thing twice.

### Sheet 2: sentences (`claims_annotator_1.csv`, `claims_annotator_2.csv`)

Each row is one sentence from an AI answer, with the records it cites shown next to it. The
checker fills two columns.

`claim_type`, what kind of sentence it is:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `observation` | States what the records contain or show |
| `interpretation` | Goes further: a trend, a cause, a general conclusion |
| `evidence_statement` | A remark about the evidence itself, e.g. "the sample is small" |

`support`, judged against the cited records **only**:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `supported` | The cited records clearly back the sentence |
| `partial` | Part of it is backed, part goes beyond the records |
| `unsupported` | No citation, or the records do not back it |
| `cannot_judge` | The record information is not enough to decide (explain in `note`) |

The full instructions are in `annotation/ANNOTATION_GUIDE.md`.

## Why "blind"?

The rows are shuffled, and the sheets do not say which search found a record or wrote a
sentence. If a checker knew that a record came from "the clever search C", they might
unconsciously rate it higher. The answer key is kept in the files `KEY_relevance.csv` and
`KEY_claims.csv`. **Only the study lead should open those**, and checkers should not read the
[Question by question](questions.qmd) or [AI answers](ai-answers.qmd) pages until they have
finished.

Two people judge everything so that we can measure how much they **agree**. If two careful
people often disagree, the judgement is hard and the results should be read with care.

## How to finish

1. Give each checker their own sheet (`..._annotator_1.csv` to one person, `..._annotator_2.csv`
   to the other). They can open it in Excel or LibreOffice, but must save it as CSV again.
2. Each checker works alone and fills in every row.
3. Put the filled sheets back in `results/final/annotation/` with the same file names.
4. Calculate the scores and update this report:

```bash
# in the heritageRAG folder
Rscript scripts/annotation.R score results/final
# in the report's folder
Rscript prepare_data.R ../heritageRAG/results/final ../heritageRAG/results/batch-pilot
quarto render
```

Plan for the time it takes: at about 30 seconds a record and 45 seconds a sentence, one person
needs roughly **`r num((n_rel * 0.5 + n_cl * 0.75) / 60, 1)` hours** in total.

## Results

```{r}
#| results: asis
if (!scored) {
  callout("note", "No judgements yet",
          "When the sheets are filled in and scored, this section shows: how often the top records of each search were useful; how well each search ranked useful records first; whether the records only search C found were useful; how much the two checkers agreed; and how many of the AI's sentences were supported.")
} else {
  cat("### Were the records useful?\n\n")
  r <- rel_sum
  tbl_out <- data.frame(Search = cond_short[r$condition],
                        `Useful (1 or 2)` = pct(r$precision_at_k), `Directly useful (2)` = pct(r$highly_relevant_share),
                        `Average score (0-2)` = num(r$mean_relevance, 2), `Good order (0-1)` = num(r$ndcg_at_k, 2),
                        `Useful among records A missed` = pct(r$not_in_A_relevant_share), check.names = FALSE)
  cat(paste(knitr::kable(tbl_out, row.names = FALSE), collapse = "\n"), "\n\n")
  cat("*Good order* is close to 1 when the useful records come first in the list.\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("**Agreement between the checkers:** they gave exactly the same number for %s of the records. The agreement score (kappa, where 0 means no better than chance and 1 means perfect) is %s.\n\n",
              pct(rel_agr$exact_agreement[1]), num(rel_agr$kappa[1], 2)))
}
if (claims_scored) {
  cat("### Were the AI's sentences supported?\n\n")
  cc <- cl_cond
  out <- data.frame(Search = cond_short[cc$condition], Sentences = cc$claims, Supported = pct(cc$supported_share),
                    Partly = pct(cc$partial_share), Unsupported = pct(cc$unsupported_share),
                    `Unsupported interpretations` = pct(cc$unsupported_interpretation_share), check.names = FALSE)
  cat(paste(knitr::kable(out, row.names = FALSE), collapse = "\n"), "\n\n")
  ag <- cl_agr[cl_agr$label == "support", ]
  cat(sprintf("**Agreement on support:** %s identical; kappa %s.\n\n", pct(ag$exact_agreement[1]), num(ag$kappa[1], 2)))
}
```
